comparison.objective: Candidate sets a gripper’s adjustable opening stop to 90°, secures it with a jam nut, and verifies retained jaw motion over repeated cycles. PR-2248 instead positions a gauge block, closes a micrometer to measurement contact using its ratchet, and locks the reading.
comparison.physical_skill: Candidate tests simultaneous driver counterholding and wrench tightening so locknut reaction does not disturb a screw setting, followed by tool withdrawal and articulated cycling. PR-2248 tests precise block placement, ratchet-only contact with counted slip clicks, avoidance of thimble overtravel, and lock-lever actuation; it does not require concentric two-tool countertorque.
comparison.success_condition: Candidate requires opening-angle accuracy, seated/retained nuts, three repeat cycles with limited stop drift, and hands-off clearance. PR-2248 requires the block remain aligned between the faces, a 20.000 mm gap tolerance, at least three valid ratchet clicks, lever locking, no squeeze or fall, and hands-off stability. Missing details: candidate hardware dimensions and torque/friction parameters remain future declared assumptions, while PR-2248 explicitly does not model the ratchet torque limit; neither omission obscures the different tested outcomes.
comparison.reason: Although both involve setting and locking an adjustable mechanism, the candidate’s defining ability is preserving a screw-set gripper stop against jam-nut reaction and proving cyclic retention, whereas PR-2248’s defining ability is controlled micrometer contact through ratchet slip and measurement locking.
